trajectory_summary: The call opens with an unusually pre-sold, eager customer who essentially asks the rep to just come install solar, but the conversation drifts into an unstructured back-and-forth about trees, satellite imagery, and tangential personal stories (his brother's trailer, cars in the yard) with no verify section, no bill flip, and no locked appointment. The call ends on a soft, passive note with the customer sounding tired and no date/time secured.
outcome_dispute: The v1 tag is unknown, but based on the transcript this should be classified as a callback/no_appointment, not a booked or tentative appointment — the rep never states a specific day or time, only 'we can kinda figure out a time over text.'

primary_coaching_focus.topic: closing an already-sold customer without a locked appointment
primary_coaching_focus.quote: just send me a photo when you can. We'll start on our end, and then we can kinda figure out a time over text. Would that work for you?
primary_coaching_focus.why: This customer opened the call asking the rep to come install solar and disclosed a $2,300 bill unprompted — about as strong a lead as a setter will get — yet the call ends with no day, no time, and no button-up mechanics at all. This is the single highest-leverage fix: the rep needs a habit of locking a specific day/time before the call ends, regardless of what logistics (photos, tree removal) are still pending.
